Giunti 6.5 - Si trova al posto giusto al momento giusto, insaccando il tiro sbilenco, diventato assist, di Fusi. Dall’80’ Cocchi sv.

Fusi 6 - Tanto dinamismo e voglia nella sua partita. Ci abbina anche un assist, quasi sicuramente involontario, a coronare una prestazione buona, macchiata solamente dal giallo che gli farà saltare la prossima. Dal 70’ Zuelli 5.5 - Ha sui piedi un’occasione potenziale quando calcia al volo in area, trovando però una deviazione che gli nega qualsiasi velleità di gol.

Pompetti 5.5 - Si spende moltissimo, ma è spesso fuori dal gioco, poco coinvolto nella manovra.

Varas 5.5 - Si fa trovare spesso e volentieri nell’area di rigore avversaria, invadendo e cercando di creare superiorità con i suoi inserimenti. Ha un paio di occasioni, ma le vanifica. Dall’85’ Bortolussi sv.

Seghetti 5.5 - Svaria moltissimo nel fronte offensivo, ma questo lo porta via dall’area. Il risultato è che l’attaccante in zona gol si vede pochissimo. Dall’80’ Di Mariano sv.

Moro 4.5 - Ha sulla testa un’occasione colossale quando stacca da solo sul cross di Zanimacchia. Un errore pesante, che costa almeno un punto ai suoi.

Allenatore: Padovano (Calabro squalificato) 5.5 - Il Padova parte male, poi ritorna e domina per larghi tratti con un palleggio più che convincente. Nel finale però si scioglie e perde una partita che avrebbe potuto anche vincere.

Krastev 6 - Non ha colpe sul gol. Poi quando viene chiamato in causa, risponde presente senza essere chiamato a grandi interventi.

Mbabu 6.5 - Mette a referto un altro assist con un cross dolcissimo per la testa di Mezzotero. Dalla sua parte arrivano i maggiori pericoli. Mette in campo tutta la sua esperienza e si rende utilissimo alla squadra. Peccato per l’infortunio che gli fa chiudere anzitempo la gara. Dal 75’ Lauritsen sv.

Ravanelli 6 - Solido. Copre bene su Seghetti e Moro, senza soffrire la velocità nella manovra biancorossa.

Delli Carri 6 - Inizio di gara impacciato e lento. Poi cresce, ma soffre sempre in marcatura su Moro. Nel finale è bravo a spazzare ogni pericolo

Meijer 5.5 - Da quella parte Zanimacchia gli fa venire il mal di testa: è alla prima da titolare e deve entrare in ritmo. D’Angelo infatti gli concede solo un tempo. Dal 46’ Gartenmann 6 - Entra e il Padova non crea più i pericoli del primo tempo. Adattato da terzino si comporta comunque benissimo.

Makoumbou 6 - Abbina corsa e contrasti inseguendo chiunque gli si pari davanti, sbaglia forse troppo con la palla tra i piedi, toccandola troppe volte e rallentando la manovra.

Abildgaard 6 - Mediano nel centrocampo di D’Angelo, smista bene ed è bravo nei contrasti, aiutando molto i difensori.

Henderson 5.5 - Gara di sostanza, macchiata da un giallo ingenuo, che gli farà saltare l’importante sfida contro la Cremonese. Dal 71’ Depaoli sv.

Mezzotero 7 - Segna un gol da attaccante purissimo girando di testa un bel cross di Mbabu, poi bissa girando in porta il servizio di Insigne. Ai due gol abbina tecnica e fisicità al servizio della squadra. Partita totale la sua: ne sentiremo parlare.

Tutino 6 - Svaria tantissimo nel fronte offensivo, scambia bene con i compagni e fa sudare i suoi marcatori. Ha anche una grande palla gol per il 2-1, ma Sorrentino lo ipnotizza. Dal 63’ Insigne 6.5 - Cambia la partita con la sua enorme qualità. Prima accende

Begic 6 - Vivace, ma troppo fumoso nell’ultima decisione. Quando si accende trova spesso la superiorità per i suoi, ma non è lucido nelle scelte. Dal 71’ Verschaeren sv.

Allenatore: D’Angelo 6.5 - La sua Sampdoria parte benissimo: pressing alto e verticalità mettono in grande crisi il Padova. Poi cala fisiologicamente dal punto di vista fisico, ma nel finale trova energie insperate anche grazie ai cambi, che permettono ai suoi di centrare il quarto successo di fila.

#2082. 24-year-old proves he can ease Kim Hellberg’s worries after starring in Middlesbrough’s win over Swansea City

Middlesbrough maintained their place at the top of the Championship table on Tuesday night as they defeated managerless Swansea City. It marked back-to-back wins for Boro after the return from the international break, following a 2-0 triumph over Bristol City on Saturday.

Kim Hellberg’s side won 2-1 against the Swans, with Myles Peart-Harris opening the scoring before Joseph Opoku’s equaliser. Star striker Will Lankshear was back amongst the goals to net the second and secure the three points.

As well as scoring the first, midfielder Peart-Harris set up Lankshear’s winner. The 24-year-old started for Middlesbrough and his performance will have come as reassurance for Hellberg given his recent midfield blows.

Earlier this week, Hellberg expressed a desire to reinforce his midfield in the January transfer window. Middlesbrough have lost Rokas Pukstas and Connor Barron to injury, meaning that the only natural players in a deeper role are usual starters Aidan Morris and Sebastian Berhalter.

Peart-Harris, like Riley McGree, can and has played in a deeper role, but is more effective further forward. However, the former Oxford United and Brentford man showed his quality alongside Morris against Swansea City.

Hellberg’s tactics mean Peart-Harris was able to progress into advanced areas. He was lurking in the 18-yard box before being found by Neto Borges’ pull-back and cleverly side-footing into the bottom corner.

For Lankshear’s goal, Peart-Harris just about beat the Swans’ offside trap and ran through before squaring it for the striker to convert. Both goals showed the freedom he had to advance, despite being down as one of Hellberg’s deeper midfield players on paper.

He was able to progress the ball with strong running and forward-thinking passing when in deeper areas. Peart-Harris spent much of the game operating on the right-hand side of the middle third of the pitch, and he was effective for Boro.

Hellberg’s lack of depth in midfield is a justified concern, especially coming into the hectic festive schedule. However, Peart-Harris’ performance against Swansea City showed he is ready to step in for Middlesbrough when Morris and Berhalter need a rest.

It was his best display in a Boro shirt to date, and if he can maintain a high level, he’ll be a valuable squad player to have throughout a demanding 2026/27 promotion push.

The performance doesn’t decrease the need for another midfielder, but it shows that Hellberg should be able to deal with the shortage until the opportunity to sign a reinforcement arises.

#2081. Glasner bacchetta il Forest: "Diversi giocatori non parlano inglese. Gli standard non sono alti"

Oliver Glasner non usa giri di parole per descrivere la situazione trovata al Nottingham Forest. Alla vigilia della sfida di Premier League contro il Chelsea, l'allenatore austriaco ha ammesso che gli standard all'interno del club non erano all'altezza delle ambizioni della società, sottolineando la necessità di un cambiamento culturale. Il Forest occupa attualmente una posizione appena sopra la zona retrocessione, con appena due vittorie nelle prime undici giornate di campionato, e il tecnico ritiene che il percorso di crescita richiederà ancora tempo.

Glasner ha individuato nell'assenza di standard condivisi uno dei principali problemi del club. "La stabilità in un'azienda nasce dagli standard. Chiunque arrivi deve impegnarsi a rispettarli. Onestamente, quando sono arrivato non erano abbastanza alti", ha dichiarato. L'austriaco ha poi affrontato anche il tema dell'integrazione dei calciatori stranieri: "Abbiamo giocatori che sono qui da quattro anni e non parlano inglese. Se vai in Italia, dopo tre mesi i giocatori rilasciano già le interviste in italiano. Se voglio allenare in Inghilterra devo parlare inglese, se voglio allenare in Italia devo parlare italiano. Altrimenti, Oliver Glasner, se vuoi parlare nel tuo dialetto, resta a casa in Austria, dove tutti ti capiscono, ma da nessun'altra parte".

L'allenatore ha ribadito che il progetto del Nottingham Forest è quello di diventare una squadra stabilmente in grado di lottare nella parte sinistra della classifica di Premier League. "Siamo ancora a qualche passo da quell'obiettivo, ma sappiamo quali passi dobbiamo compiere. Questa è una stagione di transizione: restiamo ambiziosi, ma ci sono ancora molti problemi da risolvere". Nei giorni scorsi Glasner ha inoltre incontrato a Londra il proprietario Evangelos Marinakis per pianificare il mercato di gennaio. "Mi ha chiesto di cosa abbiamo bisogno per migliorare la squadra, lo staff e l'ambiente. Vuole il meglio per il Nottingham Forest. È stato un incontro molto positivo e ne è valsa la pena affrontare sei ore di viaggio", ha concluso il tecnico.

#2079. Verso Torino-Lazio: tutte le novità sugli infortuni dei granata

Tra infortuni e il caso Rodriguez, il tecnico granata attende risposte dal campo prima della sfida contro la Lazio.

In vista della sfida tra Torino e Lazio, valida per la 13ª giornata di campionato, l'infermeria porta diversi dubbi in casa granata. Come riportato da Toro News, Abate deve valutare vari acciacchi emersi dopo Napoli e situazioni da chiarire tra difesa e fasce, pur con qualche buona notizia, e le ultime indicazioni sul campionato arriveranno direttamente dalle parole del tecnico prima del match.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Restano forti dubbi sull'impiego di Rafik Belghali contro la Lazio: il ginocchio destro infiammato (senza lesioni a menisco e legamenti) lo ha costretto al cambio al 40' al Maradona dopo aver stretto i denti al rientro anticipato dalla nazionale, e solo Abate chiarirà se potrà correre senza dolore. Stop più lungo per Ardian Ismajli: uscito nella ripresa a Napoli per una lesione di primo grado agli adduttori della coscia sinistra, salterà almeno tre settimane, a cui si somma l'operazione di osteosintesi alla mano destra per il quarto metacarpo che impone massima cautela.

Sulla sinistra resta in bilico Cristiano Biraghi, fermo a lavorare a parte per un affaticamento muscolare che lo staff valuterà giorno per giorno senza forzare, con convocazione incerta anche per la panchina. Segnali positivi invece da Niccolò Fortini, che ha superato la pubalgia ed è già tornato in panchina a Napoli: sta seguendo un percorso di potenziamento per ritrovare ritmo, e spetterà al tecnico decidere se impiegarlo con la Lazio o attendere ancora.

Il caso di Ricardo Rodriguez non è solo medico: dopo il recupero dall'infortunio pre Monza, ha risposto alla Svizzera giocando durante la sosta, attirando la dura reazione del Torino che lo ha escluso per motivi disciplinari a Napoli (scelta su cui Abate non ha avuto potere decisionale). Fisicamente sembra recuperato, ma resta da capire se verrà reintegrato per la sfida con i biancocelesti.

#2076. Gattuso ha "regalato" più di 100 milioni a Lotito

Il presidente Lotito ha trovato un tesoro. Quello che gli ha "regalato" Gennaro Gattuso con il fantastico inizio di stagione della Lazio. Delle difficoltà di un mercato estivo a costo zero non c'é traccia dopo questa prima parte di campionato. Il tecnico ha valorizzato tutto il materiale umano che gli è stato messo a disposizione. Vecchio e nuovo. Il boom economico, in questo caso, va a braccetto con i formidabili risultati sportivi. proprio quello di cui aveva bisogno il patron Lotito per uscire da una situazione a a dir poco complessa,

Proviamo a fare qualche esempio di questo "titolo Lazio" che sta volando. Il primo nome può essere quello del portiere, Mandas. Come ricordano le statistiche uno dei top della Serie A. Acquistato per un milione di euro oggi ne vale almeno 20. E vista la carenza di portieri di valore stiamo parlando di un "titolo" che potrebbe ancora crescere. Stesso discorso per il centrocampista Taylor che ha visto in questi primi cinque mesi raddoppiare e forse anche di più la sua quotazione passando dai 17 milioni di investimento ai quasi 40 di valutazione. E cosa dire di Isaksen pagato da Lotito 12 milioni e oggi quotato 30 milioni.

Le buone notizie per la Lazio coinvolgono altri giocatori. Da Floriani Mussolini cresciuto nel vivaio e oggi valutato 15 milioni, a Provstgaard che con i bonus costerà alla Lazio quattro milioni e oggi ne vale 20 a Noslin che ha visto raddoppiare la sua quotazione (da 15 investiti a 30). Plusvalenze positive arrivano anche da Doekhi, Diogo Leite, Pedraza, Dele Bashiru. Anche uno degli ultimi arrivati il centravanti Pinamonti ha visto crescere il valore del suo cartellino. Gattuso ha compiuto anche questo piccolo miracolo sportivo-economico. E ora si aspetta una ricompensa. Quale? Che nessuna delle stelle biancoceleste sia ceduta nel mercato invernale.

#2075. Blackpool managerial race takes surprise turn as 33-year-old emerges as leading contender after recent retirement

Conor Coady announced his retirement at the start of the month to turn his attention towards coaching. He is currently an assistant coach for the England U21s side, but Blackpool could offer him a first club role.

The Tangerines are searching for a new permanent manager after Ian Evatt’s dismissal last week. They sit 20th in the League One table at present with 13 points to their name in 15 games.

Reporter Pete O’Rourke states that Coady is emerging as a ‘top contender’ for the job at Bloomfield Road. He is said to have impressed FA officials early on in the England youth setup and could earn a club role as a result.

Following a run of one victory in 10 league outings, Steve Thompson stepped in for his third spell as caretaker boss and has overseen a defeat to Wigan Athletic and a draw with Leicester City.

At 33, Coady would become the second-youngest manager in the EFL, marginally older than Southampton’s Tonda Eckert. He might not have pedigree in the dugout, but he would bring a wealth of experience from an illustrious playing career.

Best remembered for an incredibly fruitful eight-year stint at Wolves, Coady asserted himself at the heart of their backline as he played an influential role in their back-to-back 7th-place finishes in 2018/19 and 2019/20.

Having captained Wolves to the Championship title and in subsequent UEFA Europa League campaigns, the ex-Liverpool youngster became renowned for his vocal leadership and infectious personality as he quickly established himself as a fan favourite at Molineux.

A move into coaching felt inevitable and he has impressed in the Three Lions’ setup since joining in September. He is passing on his wealth of experience to the next generation, and it could serve him well in a lead role.

Coady has only been involved in coaching for a matter of months, and a move to Blackpool would be the definition of being thrown in at the deep end.

With the prospect of relegation to League Two for the first time since 2017 looming large, the Tangerines are a club divided and there will be pressure to immediately deliver results if he joins.

Taking on his first managerial role in the midst of a relegation dogfight would be a tough task for Coady, particularly with a free-falling side who have shown little signs of building upon last season’s 13th-placed finish.

However, the Blackpool hierachy will certainly take encouragement from fellow strugglers Bromley’s recent upturn in form after parting company with Andy Woodman in favour of Karl Robinson, hoping similar success can be emulated at Bloomfield Road.

Villarreal ancora nel segno di Tajon Buchanan. Dopo i 2 gol in questa prima parte della Liga spagnola, arriva anche il primo sigillo in Champions League. Il giocatore ex Inter è stato decisivo per la vittoria della squadra contro lo Slavia Praga. Ma l’Inter controlla ancora Buchanan?

Il canadese è stato autentica meteora all'Inter ma nel Villarreal è tornato protagonista. Ma l'Inter ha ancora, in qualche modo, il controllo sul giocatore? La risposta è no: la cessione è stata a titolo definitivo ma con percentuale sulla futura rivendita.

In particolare, è stata una cessione a titolo definitivo, sulla base di 9 milioni di euro più il 20% sulla futura rivendita: queste le condizioni dell’operazione. L’Inter ha dunque una percentuale sulla rivendita dell’esterno, ma non lo controlla più.

#2070. Latest on John Eustace’s future as Derby County drop to bottom of the Championship

Derby County have dropped to the foot of the Championship table after a 3-0 loss to Wolves on Tuesday night. The defeat, paired with Preston North End’s thumping win over Cardiff City, has left DCFC in a dire position.

The Rams have now lost four of the last five games and won just twice in 17 league matches. John Eustace is under serious pressure, but BBC Radio Derby reporter Dominic Dietrich says that, at present, the expectation is that the 47-year-old remains in charge for Saturday’s game against Watford.

Eustace had Derby County in the fight for a Championship play-off spot last season, but a dismal 2026/27 campaign to date has left his position in peril. Injuries have hampered his squad but patience is running out among supporters.

It appears that Derby County are sticking by Eustace for now, but he is facing a level of pressure that he has arguably never encountered in his managerial career to date. His Birmingham City sacking was a big shock, and he was scarcely in danger during his strong spell as Blackburn Rovers boss.

Although back-to-back defeats have worsened the Rams’ position while fellow strugglers are picking up points, the strength of schedule may be keeping him in place. After beating Bolton Wanderers, DCFC have had to face two top Championship sides in Southampton and Wolves – both away from home as well.

The Watford clash this weekend is a far more winnable one. The Hornets have named Edward Iordanescu as their new boss but are widely viewed as a firm relegation candidate this term.

If DCFC are beaten by them, it could be the final nail in the coffin for Eustace. A draw might not even be enough.

Derby County’s dismal season means calls for Eustace’s sacking are inevitable. However, the pressure grows when fellow strugglers take action.

And, as of Wednesday afternoon, four of the Championship’s current bottom five have changed boss. Burnley, Preston North End, Watford and now Lincoln City have all parted ways with their manager or head coach – DCFC are the only ones not to make a change.

Preston have found improved form with seven points from the last three games. As relegation rivals make changes and start to pick up important results, the Rams’ fingers will be hovering above the trigger if Eustace can not turn around the club’s fortunes.

#2069. New twist in Ernie Weaver’s situation as Sheffield Wednesday revive National League loan plan

Sheffield Wednesday prospect Ernie Weaver has made a positive impression when selected for first-team football, but the depth at centre-back means there has been regular talk over a potential loan exit. Injuries changed plans previously, but now, the SWFC talent is now set to head out.

Reporting for The Wednesday Word, Joe Crann states that Weaver is not in Dave Challinor’s immediate plans and a temporary move will be sanctioned. The National League awaits, and it is most likely that the 20-year-old links up with Hornchurch, who sits 12th in the table under the management of Daryl McMahon.

Forest Green Rovers were interested in signing Weaver when he was lined up for a move earlier in the campaign. The Sheffield-born starlet is out of contract at Hillsborough at the end of this season.

Weaver’s initially planned loan was called off when he was needed for first-team cover. He stepped in and delivered a strong performance against Cambridge United and started the following game against Blackpool too.

However, he has been left out of the last two League One matchday squads. Many among the SWFC faithful believe he is deserving of a more prominent senior role given the standard of his performances when he does play, but Challinor appears to favour his more experienced defenders.

It marks an important stint for Weaver, who will be eager to show just why he’s held in such high regard. He will benefit from playing first-team football week in, week out as he continues to develop.

Weaver has given a good account of himself in both Championship and League One football when needed at Sheffield Wednesday. He drew Premier League interest early on in his first-team emergence and is widely viewed as a great prospect.

As such, he will be backed for success in the National League. A stern physical challenge awaits, but Weaver shows a love for defending and a desire to get stuck in that does go amiss in the modern game.

SWFC will be watching Weaver’s performances closely, and they will not hesitate to bring him back if injury strikes. A strong stint with Hornchurch – or whoever ends up landing him, could bring about an opportunity in the EFL in 2027.

It could also prompt interest in a permanent deal, as Weaver will be available as a free agent if a new Wednesday contract is not signed before the end of the season.

#2068. The last 7 permanent Rochdale AFC managers ranked from worst to best

It is fair to say it has been a difficult start to life back in League Two for Rochdale.

Despite missing out on the National League title last season after a heartbreaking final day draw with York City, Rochdale secured promotion back to the EFL following a three-year absence after a dramatic play-off final victory over Boreham Wood.

However, just a few weeks after Dale's Wembley success, head coach Jimmy McNulty departed the club to take over at League One side Stockport County, with Ian Watson making the move from National League North side South Shields to replace him.

Unfortunately for Watson, his tenure at the Crown Oil Arena proved to be short-lived, with Rochdale making the decision to part company with the 40-year-old on Sunday after a poor run of form left them just above the League Two relegation zone.

As Dale begin their search for Watson's replacement, we looked back and ranked the club's last seven permanent managers from worst to best.

After his reign came to an end, it is unlikely that many Rochdale fans will hold positive memories of Watson's time at the club.

Watson's South Shields side narrowly missed out on the National League North title to AFC Fylde last season before losing to Kidderminster Harriers in the play-off final, so he looked to be an exciting appointment for the Dale this summer after his impressive work in non-league.

However, the jump up two divisions proved to be too much for Watson, who won just six of his 22 games in charge, drawing three and losing 13, and, as well as the poor results, the lack of a clear style of play and his decision to sideline some of last season's promotion-winning team in favour of his own signings attracted criticism from the fanbase.

It was always going to be tough for anyone to fill McNulty's shoes, particularly for a manager with no previous EFL experience, but Watson's spell at the Crown Oil Arena is one that all parties will be keen to forget.

When Rochdale poached John Coleman from Accrington Stanley in January 2012, it was viewed as something of a coup for the club.

Coleman had established a reputation as one of the best lower league managers during his 13-year stint at Accrington, taking the reformed club into the EFL for the first time in 2006 before building a consistently competitive League Two side.

Having earned his stripes in the fourth tier, the move to Rochdale offered Coleman the chance to show what he could do at League One level, but after taking over with the club sitting towards the bottom of the table, he was unable to prevent their relegation.

Given his strong League Two record, Dale stuck with Coleman following relegation, but the expected promotion push failed to materialise, and the 63-year-old was sacked midway through the campaign in January 2013 after winning just 15 of his 52 games in charge, drawing 12 and losing 25.

After a nightmare start to the 2022-23 season, Rochdale turned to League Two survival expert Jim Bentley.

Dale had picked up just one point from their first six league games and were bottom of the table when Bentley arrived, but the 50-year-old had navigated plenty of fourth tier relegation battles during his eight-and-a-half year spell at Morecambe, so he looked to have the credentials to keep the club in the division.

Bentley inspired an initial upturn in form after taking over at the Crown Oil Arena to lift Rochdale out of the bottom two, but it was not long until their fortunes declined again, resulting in his dismissal in March 2023 with the club sitting 10 points from safety with eight games remaining.

While Bentley won just seven of his 36 games in charge, drawing seven and losing 22, it would be unfair to put too much blame on him for Dale's eventual relegation to the National League given the on and off-field issues he experienced during his tenure.

After their relegation from League One, Rochdale handed Robbie Stockdale his first senior managerial role in the summer of 2021.

Stockdale had spells as a coach with the likes of Grimsby Town, Sunderland, Hibernian and West Bromwich Albion prior to taking over at the Crown Oil Arena, and Dale would have hoped he could translate his coaching potential into success in the dugout.

Rochdale supporters may have been hoping Stockdale could lead them to promotion from League Two at the first attempt, but the club's limited budget meant that was always going to be unlikely, and the 46-year-old oversaw an underwhelming 18th-placed finish in his debut season.

After Dale lost their opening four games of the 2022-23 season, Stockdale was sacked after just over a year in charge, departing having won 16, drawn 18 and lost 25 of his 59 games at the helm.

Many notable teams have been emotionally exhausting to support in League Two, but which club tops our list at this moment in time?

Brian Barry-Murphy scored one goal and provided 11 assists in 77 appearances for Rochdale after joining from near neighbours Bury in July 2010, but his on-field exploits would only be the start of a lengthy association with the club.

In addition to his playing duties, Barry-Murphy took up a coaching role at the Crown Oil Arena in 2013, and he stepped in as caretaker manager in March 2019 following the departure of Keith Hill before being handed the permanent job the folllowing month.

Barry-Murphy successfully kept Dale in League One in the 2018-19 and 2019-20 seasons, but he was unable to repeat the trick for a third time in the 2020-21 campaign as his side were relegated, but they certainly did not go down without a fight.

In their relegation season, Rochdale were known as one of the great entertainers in the third tier, and they scored an impressive total of 61 goals throughout the campaign, but defensive frailities ultimately cost Barry-Murphy's men as they also conceded 78 goals.

Barry-Murphy won 35 of his 109 games in charge of Dale prior to his exit in the summer of 2021, drawing 25 and losing 49, but while relegation remains a black mark on the Irishman's CV, supporters of his former club may not be surprised by the subsequent success he has achieved with Cardiff City.

After making 237 appearances during an eight-year spell at the Crown Oil Arena, Jimmy McNulty is another former Rochdale player who went on to manage the club.

McNulty had two caretaker stints in charge of Dale in the 2022-23 season following the dismissals of Stockdale and Bentley, and while he was unable to prevent the club from dropping out of the EFL for the first time in their history, the improved end-of-season form under his guidance was enough to earn him the permanent job.

Rochdale finished 11th and fourth in the National League respectively during McNulty's first two seasons in charge before accumulating a remarkable 106-point haul last season, but although that was not enough to beat York to the title, they sealed a deserved promotion back to League Two with a penalty shootout victory over Boreham Wood at Wembley.

McNulty departed in June to take over at another of his former clubs in Stockport, but the 41-year-old delivered some unforgettable moments during his tenure, which saw him win 80, draw 35 and lose 43 of his 158 games in charge.

Who do you think is the best of Rochdale's recent permanent managers? Tell us in the comments below!

While McNulty produced one of the most memorable campaigns in Rochdale history last season, many supporters will agree that Keith Hill will go down as the club's best manager in recent times.

Hill first took caretaker charge of Dale in December 2006 before being given the permanent job the following month, and he led the club to promotion to League One in the 2009-10 season before making the move to Championship side Barnsley in June 2011.

The 57-year-old returned to the Crown Oil Arena for a second spell in January 2013, and he guided Rochdale to promotion from League Two once again in the 2013-14 campaign before overseeing their record finish of eighth in League One the following season.

There were plenty of other notable highlights during Hill's second stint, including a 2-2 draw at home to Premier League giants Tottenham Hotspur in the FA Cup fifth round in the 2017-18 season which earned a replay at Wembley, as well as a miraculous escape from relegation in the same campaign.

Across his two spells as Rochdale manager, Hill won 242, drew 131 and lost 197 of his 570 games in charge, and his legacy at the club will be secure for a long time to come.

#2067. Dave Challinor drops Sheffield Wednesday transfer hint - Owls are missing something

Dave Challinor has issued a clear transfer message after just three games as Sheffield Wednesday's new head coach, with the January window now just over one month away from opening.

The Owls' winning start to League One life under the former Stockport County boss was halted by a goalless draw against last season's play-off semi-finalists, Stevenage, at the SPORTA Arena on Tuesday.

Wednesday are currently fourth in the table, having taken 27 points from their first 16 encounters, just five less than Challinor's former employers who top the standings.

The upcoming window is just the second of the Arise Capital era at Hillsborough, and the first in which the 51-year-old will be reunited with former Stockport chief, Simon Wilson, who is now the Steel City side's sporting director.

However, it feels rather apparent that Challinor has already dropped a transfer hint to the hierarchy.

Wednesday's squad have certainly shared their 27 goals so far this season around, with Jamal Lowe currently topping the individual charts with seven.

When all fit and available, Challinor has plenty of attacking options at his disposal, including Ali Al-Hamadi, Harry Gray, Mason Burstow, Davis Keillor-Dunn and Louie Barry.

Yet, whilst Keillor-Dunn has impressed in recent weeks with his own four-goal haul, the Owls boss has admitted that the club lacks a natural centre-forward ahead of the January window.

“We definitely are,” he stated. “With Ali being out, he's (Keillor-Dunn) probably the closest. Harry, I think, will develop into a nine. But as an 18-year-old playing in League One, the physical part of that tour is going to be tough for him.

“They are hard to come by because a number nine, you're looking for the complete centre-forward, aren't you? Somebody that can hold the ball up when you go up to them, is an aerial threat, still wants to be able to run behind, gets themselves in the box when a cross is coming in," he added.

"Difficult to find if I was looking for them. I hope that we get the answers from what we've already got in the building, but we've got time to time to judge that.”

Despite the attraction Wednesday have in League One in terms of stature, realising such transfer wishes could be difficult for the South Yorkshire side to realise.

Keillor-Dunn's short-term loan from Wrexham is a prime example, as, irrespective of the 28-year-old's quality in the division, only an agreement until January could be struck due to budgeting restraints, with the club still working under a strict business plan from the EFL having exited administration in the summer.

An unwanted return to the Racecourse Ground from the Owls' perspective could free up much-needed funds, but with the January window notoriously hard for doing business in, there are no guarantees that Challinor can solve such a conundrum with players from elsewhere.

The potential sale of Huddersfield’s Joe Taylor could really shake up the League One promotion race.

There is a consensus amongst Wednesdayites that more quality is needed in attack, despite the blend of experience and energy which is at Challinor's disposal.

Five goals within his first two league encounters against Plymouth Argyle and Barnsley demonstrates exactly what this squad is capable of, but despite having six attempts on target against Stevenage, none of Keillor-Dunn, Barry, the returning Al-Hamadi and Jamal Lowe could find target.

Owls fans, is a new striker the main priority for Dave Challinor in January? Comment below!

Burstow is set to return from a groin issue in the coming weeks, meaning that, in the short-term, at least, Wednesday are not short of options, and it would certainly be beneficial for those names to fire goals in on a regular given the lack of potential wriggle room in the transfer market.

#2065. 5 Chris Cohen & Tom Shaw replacements Lincoln City must eye ASAP

Lincoln City have confirmed the sacking of dual head coaches Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw following a disastrous run of form, with the pair having only succeeded Michael Skubala over the summer.

The Imps elected to promote internally upon Skubala's bombshell departure to Championship rivals Bristol City after guiding the side to the second-tier for the first time since 1961 by romping to the League One title, which left their key decision-makers to opt against hiring an external candidate.

Instead, Lincoln placed faith in the abilities of Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw as the duo played vital roles in the club's success under Skubala.

They would, however, ultimately fall short of continuing the Imps' upwards direction of travel, and have been relieved of their duties after a losing streak was extended to five matches by falling to a chastening 4-0 defeat at the hands of Charlton Athletic on Tuesday evening.

Lincoln have won just four of their opening 17 matches in the Championship and are positioned merely three points above 22nd-placed Preston North End, who themselves are on the rise following a three-match unbeaten streak, and with eight losses from the last ten, the second-tier newcomers simply had to make a change in order to retain prospects of achieving survival.

With Lincoln having already confirmed the initiation of a recruitment process to seek out a replacement, Football League World has decided to take a close look at FIVE candidates that the strugglers should be setting their sights on in the coming days.

Heading proceedings underway is Matt Bloomfield, who wouldn't represent the most pulse-racing or wildcard appointment in the world but could just be worth a punt from the Imps' key decision-makers.

His managerial career has been something of a rollercoaster already, with the former midfielder initially shining in charge of Wycombe Wanderers and mounting a shock title race alongside Birmingham City before leaving for Luton Town, suffering relegation from the Championship and then being dismissed out of Kenilworth Road months later.

Clearly, then, it was an ill-fated decision to leave Wycombe in the first place, and it's one which Bloomfield is perhaps yet to recover from. He wasn't able to keep Oxford United afloat after succeeding Gary Rowett either, and while the appointment of Aaron Ramsey has since proven an extremely-shrewd one, Bloomfield's sacking still felt harsh back in the summer.

A look at the 25 best-run clubs in English football according to AI chatbot ChatGPT.

Bloomfield's best work, of course, came at Wycombe, where relatively-modest expectations and financial resources during much of his tenure clearly worked in his favour. It would be rather similar with Lincoln, although the Imps' situation could also be comparable to Oxford's and the fact that he failed to keep the Yellows alive in the second-tier is an obvious caveat.

Still, Bloomfield is just 43 and has time on his side to turn his stock around - and Lincoln could do much worse than providing him that opportunity.

A much more high-risk, high-reward appointment, meanwhile, could come in the form of Calum McFarlane, who was tenuously linked with the top job at Sincil Bank over the summer.

Whether there was anything at all in those links is yesterday's news. Now, with Lincoln on the search for a new boss once again, McFarlane is somebody who should be coming under serious consideration, and he would fit the club's head-coach model much more seamlessly than other candidates.

The highly-rated Chelsea coach is currently working as Xabi Alonso's assistant after taking interim charge at Stamford Bridge during the back-end of the previous season following Liam Rosenior's departure, and has built up an encouraging reputation in West London.

Calm under pressure, progressive in his methods and experienced in coaching young talent from his days leading Chelsea's academy sides, McFarlane's stock is on the rise and Lincoln should be testing the waters to see whether a first senior, full-time gig could tempt the 41-year-old away from the Premier League giants.

These hires typically go one of two ways, but the potential upside is clear to see.

Lincoln have rarely been ones to shy away from left-field hires in the dugout, having done so with both Cohen and Shaw and the aforementioned Skubala, yet they shouldn't dismiss the possibility of taking that one step further with a more continental approach to mirror an overarching part of their player recruitment strategy.

Wilfried Nancy has never coached in England, and the Frenchman's stock has taken a notable hit following his disastrous short-lived reign at Celtic nearly a year ago. He won just two of his eight games in charge of the Hoops and departed under a cloud with the worst record of any boss on either side of the Old Firm divide, yet that alone should not completely overlook a fantastic of body of work in the MLS before jetting off across the Atlantic.

Nancy initially started off in senior coaching by succeeding Thierry Henry at CF Montreal, and finished his time with the Canada-based outfit with the second-best record in the Eastern Conference back in 2022. He went one better after joining Columbus Crew, where he would win the 2023 MLS Cup before winning the MLS Coach of the Year while earning wide plaudits for an attractive, possession-heavy brand of football.

Known for playing a 3-4-2-1 shape with interchanging roles and an emphasis on dominating the ball with attacking overloads and a high tempo both in and out of possession, Nancy follows the ilk of many modern-day head coaches by unequivocally sticking to his principles.

Many Celtic fans felt as though that was his downfall at Parkhead, whereas there would have to be questions as to whether he'd even be able to get Lincoln players to carry out such tactical and technical demands.

Nonetheless, Nancy is one of the more gifted and high-ceiling coaches that Lincoln could hire - even if it would be a wildcard call of the high-risk, high-reward genre.

Bo Henriksen's style, meanwhile, would be much more suitable for what remains a primarily pragmatic, dynamic and aggressive Imps side, yet his appointment undoubtedly represents a more ambitious call.

The Danish coach, who spent three surprising years in English football with Kidderminster Harriers and Bristol Rovers during a largely-unremarkable playing career, has earned an impressive reputation on the continent, and it's one that could just put him out of Lincoln's reach.

That's not to say that Lincoln shouldn't be asking the question, though, as Henriksen would be a superb appointment. He started off with FC Midtjylland before taking Zurich from the foot of the league table after ten games to a mid-table finish, and then earned a move to Mainz 05 as a result of his work in Switzerland.

Mainz enjoyed a rich run of form under Henriksen, who led them from relegation trouble to 13th place with a nine-match unbeaten streak at the end of the 2023/24 term. They went even better the following season and left fans across Germany shocked by reaching third place in late March, before losing their footing and settling for a UEFA Europa Conference League spot instead.

It was a strong season regardless, yet Henriksen would fall short of matching those standards and received his marching orders in December of last year following one win from his opening 12 games. Interestingly, he has been out of work ever since and Lincoln should be pulling out all the stops to seal his return to management.

Unlike Nancy, for example, Henriksen is not in the modern-day possession-heavy coaching mold and instead focuses on a high-energy approach involving intense pressing out of possession and quick transitions. He's known as something of a culture-builder, too, often instilling belief, fight and energy into struggling squads low on confidence, with those attributes earmarking him as exactly what Lincoln need right now.

Of all the listed candidates, he could just be the best pick of the lot.

The fifth and final boss who should be coming under Lincoln's consideration is Jimmy Thelin, who has been unattached since his sacking from Aberdeen in January of this year.

Thelin enjoyed success leading Elfsborg in his native Sweden between 2018 and 2024, and 2023 was a particularly notable year as he won the Allsvenskan Coach of the Year after guiding his side to an impressive third-placed finish.

That form put him on the radar of Aberdeen, who made a remarkable start under his stewardship in 2024/25 by winning 10 of his opening 11 games in charge. They did, however, take only five wins from the remaining 27 - yet still managed to win their first trophy in eleven years by beating Celtic in the Scottish Cup final.

Lincoln City fans, what do you make of FLW's selections? Who would be your number-one choice? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

Thelin never managed to sustain his early-season form at Aberdeen and was later sacked at the start of the year, which makes him a realistic yet somewhat-ambitious potential candidate for Lincoln to target.

The 48-year-old Swede, who was linked with the Sheffield Wednesday job just last month, is known to be keen on managing in England and that would only help the Imps' chances if they decided to court his services.

#2064. THE BREAKDOWN: The real reasons why Enzo Maresca's Man City can't stop losing - from anonymous Enzo Fernandez abandoning Elliot Anderson, to the fatal flaws in Italian's set-up that are being brutally exposed

Published: 07:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 14:40 EST, 20 November 2026

Diet Pep is losing his fizz. Enzo Maresca may look like Pep Guardiola, may have learned his craft under his Manchester City predecessor, but his quest to follow in his mentor’s footsteps has all gone a bit flat.

Seven successive Premier League wins to start his City reign, a record for a new manager in the competition, breaking one jointly-held by Guardiola, gave the impression that this might be a smooth passing of the torch after all.

Three months in, and three defeats on the spin that left them six points behind Arsenal have made it clear that something is not clicking for Maresca.

Is the uncertainty around the potential punishment following that guilty verdict taking its toll? Is Maresca just suffering from his usual late autumn dips? He suffered similar tricky periods around late October and early November at Leicester and his first season at Chelsea too.

Or is there something at the heart of his side, of his system, that’s finally being exposed?

Enzo Maresca's Man City have slumped to three straight Premier League defeats after a promising start to the season

Guardiola’s City was all about control. Keep the ball, dominate the pitch, play the game at your pace, on your terms.

Maresca’s City, regardless of how well they started the season, has been about anything but. It has been about triumph amid chaos, about moments of magic more than the overarching method.

Without that control, City’s defensive issues have been laid bare. The 13 goals they have let in after 10 games is their most at this stage since 2008. They haven’t kept a clean sheet in their last eight matches in all competitions. That's a drought longer than at any point under Guardiola.

Their biggest problem over City's three successive Premier League defeats is just how susceptible they have been to counter attacks.

Only Newcastle have faced more shots this season following ‘fast breaks’ – data giants Opta's term for counter attacks – than City’s 17, and 11 of those have come in the last three games: six against Nottingham Forest, two of which led to goals, three against Brighton and another two against Aston Villa.

Maresca’s side are being more profligate in possession, too. Over the first seven games of the season, they lost the ball 120 times a game on average – one of the best figures in the division. Since then, it’s closer to 140.

City have been wasteful in possession and regularly overrun on the counter, with Elliot Anderson (centre) too often left isolated in midfield

Many of these problems have their roots in Maresca's serious problems in midfield. Rodri, the best holding midfielder of his generation, was always going to be hard to replace but Maresca appears to be expecting Elliot Anderson to do it all on his own.

Anderson is at his best when he’s free to get up and down the pitch, box to box, using his physicality not just in winning the ball back but progressing it. No midfielder played more passes into the final third last season than Anderson at Forest. At one stage of the campaign, he had played more progressive passes than any other player across Europe’s top five leagues.

And yet Maresca is forcing Anderson to play as the sitter while his golden boy Enzo Fernandez, whom he pushed City to sign in the summer for £125million, is roaming free and high up the pitch.

Maresca likes his teams to build up in a 3-1-6 shape, which sees Fernandez push up as an extra attacking midfielder, and leaves Anderson manning the fort alone.

When City lose the ball, though, it leaves them wide open.

This is the opening goal City conceded against Forest. Josko Gvardiol wants to play the ball inside but has only red shirts and empty green space ahead of him. Anderson is the only man free, but even he is too high and has a Forest player ready to cut off the pass. Eventually, Gvardiol gets robbed and Forest score.

A lack of options for Josko Gvardiol (left) led to Forest's opener against City. Enzo Fernandez (circled) was caught high up the pitch, way ahead of the deeper Anderson (also circled)

Here’s another moment in the defeat by Brighton.

The Seagulls break forward on the flank and Anderson races over to close the ball down. Fernandez is, you guessed it, high up the pitch.

City have no midfield cover to stop the ball inside, Abdukodir Khusanov gets drawn in and leaves loads of space in behind for Yasin Ayari to exploit and cross to Maxim De Cuyper for a great chance.

The lack of protection offered by Anderson and especially the more advanced Fernandez was again on show against Brighton, who were able to exploit the acres of space left in midfield

Fernandez is doing what Maresca wants, but it’s not working. Maresca needs more from him, especially when Anderson’s instincts are to press and harass and bully, which can leave gaps when he does not yet read the game as comprehensively as Rodri.

Anderson sits in the top five for ball recoveries among midfielders to have played 500 minutes this season. Fernandez is in the bottom five. That figure becomes even more alarming when you consider Anderson has created more chances from open play than Fernandez, too.

Ayyoub Bouaddi showed at the World Cup that he had the most similar profile to Rodri. It might be time for Maresca to put some faith in him.

Maresca has always wanted his goalkeeper to be an 11th outfielder. In his one season at Leicester, Mads Hermansen played more passes than any goalkeeper in Championship history. During his time at Chelsea, there was a shaky moment in a draw with Arsenal when loud groans greeted a misplaced pass from Robert Sanchez.

‘I am the guy who asks Robert to do that,’ said Maresca after that game. ‘The moment he stops doing that, he is not going to play.’

Donnarumma, though, for all his (usually) excellent shot-stopping, is anything but a ball-playing goalkeeper. The ball rolled under his foot from a simple back pass against Coventry and so nearly crept over the line. He gifted France an early lead while on international duty with Italy when he passed the ball straight to Michael Olise.

Only two keepers made more errors leading to shots than Donnarumma across the course of last season, with many of those being with his feet, like when he gifted Kai Havertz an equaliser in City's victory over Arsenal in April.

Gianluigi Donnarumma has never been good with his feet - now his excellent shot-stopping has taken a dip too

The Italian should have easily dealt with Nicolas Jackson's second goal in City's 2-1 loss at Aston Villa

The decision to let James Trafford leave in the summer, especially with Guardiola’s impending departure and a manager like Maresca coming in, is looking ever more misguided.

Trafford is not immune to mistakes either, of course. He erred badly when trying to play out from the back for City against Spurs last season and made an almost identical howler for Leeds at Bournemouth in October. But he is still far more confident at playing out from the back than Donnarumma.

The double blow for Maresca is that the trade-off with Donnarumma – where he makes up for his weakness with the ball at his feet by making saves that other keepers can’t make – is no longer paying off either.

Nicolas Jackson’s shot squirmed straight through him to hand Villa victory and condemn City to their first defeat of the season.

When you are coughing up chances as frequently as City are, Maresca needs his keeper to be on top form.

Do you know who is keeping the ball out of his net? James Trafford. He boasts the highest save percentage of any goalkeeper in the top flight, keeping out 81 per cent of the shots on target coming his way. Donnarumma is 15th, on less than 66 per cent.

According to Opta’s expected data, Trafford has also prevented more than four goals that he should have conceded from the quality of the shots he’s faced. Again, he’s the best in the Premier League. Donnarumma is middle of the pack.

‘At the moment, I’m not thinking about the goalkeeping situation,’ said Maresca recently. Without Trafford there and just 34-year-old Geronimo Rulli as back-up, he doesn’t really have a choice but to persist with Donnarumma and hope he improves.

When the goals stop flowing for Erling Haaland, City can't mask all their other problems.

So used are we now to seeing the Norwegian on the scoresheet, having notched nine in City’s opening eight matches, that when he goes just two games without a goal it feels as if he’s on a barren spell.

The issue, though, is less down to Haaland and more that City’s build-up in recent weeks is struggling to get him into the game.

City are finding it more difficult to get Haaland on the ball. His touches per game are falling steadily but, crucially, so are the quality of the chances his team-mates are creating for him.

Haaland had more than one Opta-defined 'big chance' in five of City’s opening seven games. He’s had just one come his way in each of their three defeats.

His expected goals (xG) tally is dropping too. Across City’s winning streak, Haaland’s average xG per match was 0.81. Only once, against Liverpool, did it drop below 0.5.

Over the three defeats, it’s just 0.45 and has not once gone above 0.5.

Antoine Semenyo missing the last three games through injury has not helped, especially when teams now try to pack the middle of the pitch and force City wide.

Haaland will come good, he always does, but City need to start serving him again if Maresca wants to get through this tricky spell and stop the vultures from circling.

#2063. Ex-Liverpool and Wolves star enters Blackpool FC managerial frame

Former Premier League and England international defender, Conor Coady, has reportedly emerged as a leading contender to replace Ian Evatt at League One strugglers, Blackpool.

That is according to an update from Pete O'Rourke via X, with the Tangerines beginning third-tier life without their former defender with one point from a possible six.

A 2-1 loss to Lancashire rivals, Wigan Athletic, at Bloomfield Road on Saturday lunchtime was followed up by an encouraging draw against Russell Martin's in-form Leicester City on Tuesday night, with Niall Ennis equalising Will Alves' opener.

Blackpool are currently 20th in League One having taken just 13 points from 15 matches, and whilst the club still have a game in hand to play over many divisional rivals, only a two-goal swing separates them and Doncaster Rovers, who occupy the final relegation place.

Blackpool have endured mixed fortunes since their relegation from the Championship three-and-a-half years ago, with whoever replaces Evatt being the fifth head coach at Bloomfield Road since then.

Evatt was able to guide the Seasiders to a 13th-placed finish last season, ending the campaign with four wins on the bounce, but departed the club last week on his 45th birthday, and attention has now turned as to who will be his successor in the long run.

Steve Thompson led the fixtures against Wigan and Leicester, but as per O'Rourke, it has been claimed that Coady, 33, has emerged as a 'top contender' for the role, just weeks after confirming his retirement from playing.

The centre-back amassed over 300 combined appearances at Premier League and Championship level, and is best known for his spells at Liverpool, Wolves, Everton and Wrexham, which included a second-tier title win at Molineux, as well as earning 10 England caps.

It is stated that the England Under-21s assistant has already impressed higher-ups at the Football Association after landing said role two months' ago.

FLW have looked at the top 12 EFL League One clubs and have ranked them smallest to largest based on their average home attendance in the 26/27 season

Coady terminated his Wrexham contract in August after making just six appearances under Phil Parkinson at the Racecourse Ground, and immediately turned his focus to coaching.

Indeed, he was offered a role within Liverpool's academy setup, working alongside former Blackpool midfielder, Jay Spearing, before replacing Ashley Cole as part of Lee Carsley's setup with the Young Lions, who have recently won successive UEFA Under-21 European Championships.

It remains to be seen if Coady does land his first full-time managerial role on the Fylde Coast, but when asked about what the future holds, he recently said: "I'm not massively in a rush because I want to make sure it's (the decision is) right."

There has, unsurprisingly, been plenty of discourse as to who the Blackpool hierarchy will turn to next in an attempt to improve the club's fortunes.

#2062. Ashley Barnes reacts to huge moment for ex-Burnley star Maxime Esteve

Maxime Esteve made his Champions League debut for RB Leipzig against Lens on Tuesday night, and one of his former teammates was cheering him on.

One of the biggest costs that comes with relegation from the Premier League can be the loss of players that comes with it. This exodus took place at the end of the 2025-26 season for Burnley, just as it routinely does for clubs relegated from this level, and in the case of defender Maxime Esteve the offer was an appealing one. The 24-year-old centre-back signed for RB Leipzig in the summer, and although he's primarily been used as a squad player by the Bundesliga outfit through the opening weeks of this season, he was included in their team for their Champions League match against RC Lens on Tuesday night, his debut in the competition.

It turned out to be a successful night for both the player and his new club. RB Leipzig won the match 3-1, and Esteve scored strongly for his performance before being withdrawn midway through the second half with cramp. And after the match, when he posted to social media about his delight at making his Champions League debut, one of his former Burnley teammates was there in the replies with a show of support for him.

Posting to the social media platform Instagram after RB Leipzig's 3-1 win over RC Lens in the Champions League on Tuesday night, Maxime Esteve couldn't contain his delight at having made his first appearance in Europe's premier club competition, saying, "First Champions League game, at home, and a win to go with it."

Esteve was clearly very pleased to have been given the opportunity in such a prestigious tournament: "A night I won’t forget. Thanks to the team and to our fans for the atmosphere. Let’s keep going."

But an assured performance will only have strengthened his case for a more regular berth in their starting eleven.

This is an exciting time to be at the club. RB Leipzig are in fourth place in the Bundesliga, and although Bayern Munich remain the clear favourites to win the league title, Leipzig are only three points behind current leaders Borussia Dortmund.

It's all a long way removed from Burnley's dismal 2025-26 Premier League season, which ended with the Clarets relegated in 19th place having picked up just 22 points all season, leaving them 19 points short of safety.

Ashley Barnes, meanwhile, stayed at Turf Moor following relegation after agreeing another contract extension with Burnley during the summer. But Barnes has not been a central part of the Burnley team since his 2025 return to Turf Moor. He only made seven appearances for them in the Premier League last season, all of which came from the bench and which amounted to just 41 minutes of game time.

Rangers goalkeeper Ivor Pandur has revealed his 'unbelievable' experience of working under Allan McGregor.

Ivor Pandur has made an impressive start to life at Rangers after joining from Hull City

Pandur insists he is only going to keep improving under the guidance of Allan McGregor

#2058. Liverpool vs Man Utd: Preview, key stats, team news & where to watch

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Mauricio Pochettino begins his Manchester United reign with a huge test at Anfield on Sunday, with Manchester United desperate for a result after making their worst start to a top-flight season in 40 years.

Manchester United have collected just eight points from their opening 10 Premier League matches, with one win and five draws leaving them 18th in the table. They have also conceded in every league game this season and are currently on a run of 11 consecutive matches without keeping a clean sheet in all competitions.

Mauricio Pochettino only arrived to the club on Wednesday after replacing Michael Carrick, leaving him with just a few training sessions to prepare for one of the biggest fixtures in English football.

There is some encouragement for the Argentine, however. Eight of United’s last nine permanent or caretaker managers have avoided defeat in their first match in charge. That may be some encouragement to the Argentine.

Meanwhile, Liverpool are not exactly enjoying a comfortable season at home either. They sit fourth with 18 points but have won just once in their five Premier League matches at Anfield so far, giving them the third-worst home record in the Premier League.

Their recent form across all competitions stands at three wins, one draw and two defeats in their last six matches. Liverpool most recently beat Crystal Palace 3-1, but they will know that United’s poor league position does not make this fixture any less complicated.

Liverpool have received positive news ahead of Sunday’s meeting. Dominik Szoboszlai and Virgil van Dijk are both expected to feature, while Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong could also be available.

Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni have returned to team training following knee injuries but are unlikely to make the squad. Hugo Ekitike remains a long-term absentee with an Achilles problem.

Manchester United could welcome back Patrick Dorgu and Harry Maguire after both trained following fitness concerns. They were seen in that leaked drone footage as well. Lisandro Martínez is also available again after serving his suspension.

Luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford could return, although their availability remains uncertain. Carlos Baleba, Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko are still sidelined.

The new United boss has a difficult personal record against Liverpool. Pochettino has faced the Reds 19 times, winning three, drawing five and losing 11. He has also failed to win any of his last eight meetings with them in all competitions. That might be a concern, but everything has a first time.

Pochettino will be encouraged by United’s overall record against Liverpool.  United have an edge with 85 wins compared to Liverpool’s 72 across 218 meetings. Their most recent encounter also went their way, with a 3-2 victory on May 3.

However, United arrive on a disappointing run of seven consecutive away matches without a win and have managed just one victory in their last 11 games.

Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of his first United game against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, with plenty of questions surrounding the players who will benefit from his arrival.

Manchester United have struggled badly this season, sitting 18th in the Premier League after collecting just eight points from their opening 10 matches.

Pochettino replaces Michael Carrick and his job has been described as one of the toughest jobs in the Premier League. Former defender Wes Brown believes Manchester United have a chance with Pochettino to change things despite it being very difficult.

Brown believes the new manager has enough quality at his disposal to improve the situation, despite the difficult start and the pressure that comes with the Manchester United job.

Asked whether Pochettino faces an impossible task after previous managers failed to bring success to Old Trafford, Brown was confident the Argentine could make a difference.

Published: 15:10 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 15:50 EST, 20 November 2026

Antonio Conte has claimed clubs are 'frightened of winning' if they have concerns over his methods after the Italian was overlooked for the Manchester United job.

Conte had been heavily linked with the role at Old Trafford, joining Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe and Unai Emery among the list bookmakers' favourites to replace Michael Carrick.

Man United ultimately went with another former Chelsea and Tottenham boss in Mauricio Pochettino, paying around £10million in compensation to lure him away from being head coach of the United States' national team.

Conte, who remains out of work after leaving Napoli in the summer, has now hit back at reports suggesting Man United may have been put off by his intensity and demands.

'First, let me address the question of my method,' Conte told the Cronache di Spogliatoio podcast.

'If anyone is frightened by my method, then they are frightened of winning, because that methodology leads to victory. That is my answer.

Antonio Conte has claimed clubs are 'frightened of winning' if they have concerns over his methods after the Italian was overlooked for the Manchester United job

Man United opted to appoint Mauricio Pochettino as head coach after sacking Michael Carrick

Conte hit back at suggestions Man United's hierachy might have been relucant to appoint him because of his methods

'Manchester United has such a significant history that I find it strange to imagine anyone could be afraid of an approach aimed at restoring the club to its true stature.

'(United) last won the league in 2013, under Ferguson. I have immense respect for Sir Alex Ferguson.

'I've read his book, and when I was in London, I was fortunate enough to visit his home and spend a day with him. He has an incredible passion for talking about football, though, at times, his Scottish accent can be quite hard to follow.

'Through his own methodology and approach, he made Manchester United great.

'That is why I find certain remarks almost offensive toward United; it's as if someone were placing a veto on the club's return to its own history.

'A method is what's needed to achieve major results. And if you're suggesting that this method requires hard work, well, yes, it does. Everyone has to work hard, not just the players.'

Conte has long been known for his combustible personality - as well as an impressive winning record as a coach.

Conte has won five Serie A titles across three clubs and won the Premier League with Chelsea

Conte famously left Tottenham after an explosive press conference in 2023, where he labelled his players as 'selfish' and took aim at the club's culture.

The Italian, however, has overseen five Serie A title wins during his spells at Juventus, Inter Milan and Napoli, along with winning the Premier League and FA Cup with Chelsea.

It is not the first time Conte has spoken out in recent weeks following links to Old Trafford, with the 57-year-old having denied he had set 'specific conditions' about taking over at United.

La Repubblica claimed Conte wanted 'carte blanche on the transfer market' and to act as a manager, rather than a head coach, with a technical staff behind the scenes chosen by him involving 'trusted collaborators'.

'My name has been linked with numerous clubs, but there are currently no negotiations at an advanced stage,' Conte responded on social media last month.

'Following a wonderful and successful spell in charge of Napoli, I will take the time I need to consider how and when to return to management. It will be a carefully considered decision, one I will make when I believe the conditions are right.

'I have read reports of financial demands and requests for full control that I have supposedly already made to the clubs mentioned, as well as reservations about what has been described as my "strong personality". These reports are unfounded, as there is currently no concrete basis for such assessments.

'Should a concrete opportunity arise, that will be the time to hold discussions with the club concerned and jointly consider the terms of a potential agreement, with due regard for both parties' needs and the qualities and approach that define my work as a manager.'

Pochettino, who landed the job at Old Trafford, has faced a whirlwind start having flown into Manchester following his final match in charge of the United States on Tuesday.

The Argentine took training for the first time on Thursday and will lead the Red Devils out for the first time on Sunday in a blockbuster clash with Liverpool at Anfield.

Pochettino takes over with Man United lying in the Premier League's relegation zone having won just one of their opening ten matches.

Manchester United have spent approximately £95m appointing and dismissing managers since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013, according to BBC Sport, with the total expected to pass £100m following Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival.

United’s latest financial disclosures confirm a fee of £7.584m in connection with appointing Pochettino, who left his role as United States national team head coach earlier this month.

The figure takes the cumulative cost of managerial changes to around £95m, according to BBC Sport’s analysis. That total is expected to rise once the costs of Michael Carrick’s dismissal and appointing Pochettino’s coaching staff are included.

Pochettino signed a two-and-a-half-year contract on 13 November, replacing Carrick after a difficult start to the Premier League season. The club’s Stock Market filing states that the appointment fee will be recognised in its financial accounts for the current quarter. United also confirmed borrowing a further £10m on 16 November, taking the amount drawn on their revolving credit facility to £240m.

Pochettino is United’s ninth full-time managerial appointment since Ferguson’s departure, including Ralf Rangnick’s interim spell. The club have also changed managers during each of the past three seasons.

United’s financial disclosures show that their long-term debt stood at £577.4m on 30 September, while outstanding transfer-fee commitments totalled £417m. Those figures are separate from the cost of appointing and dismissing managers.

A Reuters analysis has put the wider cost of managerial and senior football staff changes above £100m, using a broader calculation. Pochettino now faces the task of improving United’s results, beginning with Sunday’s Premier League trip to Liverpool.

#2052. Middlesbrough must be shaking at one thing Tonda Eckert is doing at Southampton

The Championship has already provided some dramatic encounters this season, and many will expect nothing less when Southampton host Middlesbrough on Friday night in front of the Sky cameras.

The past six months tell you there is no love lost between Saints and Boro supporters, which will only add to the atmosphere normally generated when two sides towards the top of the table face off under the lights.

Tonda Eckert's side are just seven points behind the league leaders after 17 matches, and could narrow that gap down to four whilst, in turn, piling the pressure on Wolves, Stoke City and Birmingham City.

There is much to like about the way the German and Kim Hellberg set up their sides, with Boro the undisputed top scorers ahead of the encounter, largely through Will Lankshear's remarkable form.

However, Saints will not be fearful of the quality oozing through Hellberg's ranks, with Eckert also able to call upon several technically gifted individuals in a bid to attack the game.

Eckert is approaching the one-year anniversary of his permanent appointment as Saints head coach, and plenty has gone on since then.

Given the club's recent Premier League past, there is always an expectancy for Saints to be in and among the Championship's promotion hopefuls, and that has remained the case this term despite a four-point deduction.

Home form is seen as a key barometer in the division, and Southampton's displays at St Mary's under the 33-year-old have been almost perfect.

Friday night's clash will be the 30th home fixture Eckert has overseen, with Southampton losing just two of the previous 29 against Hull City on January 17th and to West Ham United in August.

Although Middlesbrough have accumulated one more point and played more times at the Riverside Stadium, Saints, strictly speaking, boast the division's best home record, taking 22 points from a possible 24, scoring 22 goals in the process.

Eckert, who was recently rewarded with a fresh contract, revealed in September that reconnecting with the club's fanbase has been a key reason behind such an impressive run.

As impressive as Middlesbrough have been under Hellberg, the North East outfit aren't flawless, and they were exposed in disappointing away performances and results at Wrexham and Watford.

In both encounters, Boro continued to dominate possession and created 30 openings across 180 minutes, but a lack of cutting edge, somewhat down to an injury sustained by Lankshear, was punished by Phil Parkinson's side, whilst, on another day, a side in better form than the Hornets could have performed a smash-and-grab.

Will Lankshear has sent a message to Middlesbrough fans ahead of Friday evening's hotly-anticipated clash with Southampton

Southampton have averaged 57.1% possession this season, but certainly have the firepower to expose any defensive frailties through the likes of Leo Scienza, Finn Azaz and Canadian hotshot, Cyle Larin, who was back on the goalscoring trail against Derby County.

Boro have also taken just 12 of their 35 points in away matches thus far, which could give travelling supporters further nerves heading into Friday's contest.

With both sides known for a high-tempo game, a fascinating encounter was already on the cards, but then you factor in the passion from the stands which is likely to be channeled by the 22 starters, substitutes and head coaches after May's Spygate debacle.

Hellberg revealed in October that he'd received an apology from Eckert after Southampton were found guilty of breaching EFL regulations and the German was found to have done similar against FA guidelines, but after what ensued in the play-off semi-finals, which were effectively void as Middlesbrough went on to play and lose the final to Hull City in emotionally draining circumstances, the two sets of fans are likely to be partaking in intense 'back-and-forth'.

Who comes out on top in this highly-anticipated fixture? Comment below!

Eckert will hope such feelings are used positively by his team, as one lapse in concentration could bring their unbeaten home record to an end.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#2049. Chelsea World Cup Knockout Load Gives Xabi Alonso Pre-Season Problem

Chelsea’s World Cup contingent has moved from a group-stage watchlist into a genuine Xabi Alonso planning problem.

Chelsea’s own tournament update confirms that Enzo Fernandez, Mike Penders, Moises Caicedo, Kendry Paez, Malo Gusto and Jorrel Hato have reached the Round of 32.

England have also progressed after their final Group L win over Panama, which keeps Reece James and Trevoh Chalobah inside the wider knockout picture.

For supporters, that is a status marker. For Alonso, it is where summer pride starts to become pre-season compression.

The concern is not simply volume. It is where the minutes are landing.

Enzo has not missed a minute for Argentina, while Caicedo has remained central for Ecuador and captained them in the 2-1 win over Germany.

Those are not fringe workloads. They are the two midfield profiles Chelsea have built large parts of their control game around.

Alonso’s first Chelsea pre-season was always going to demand clarity through the middle of the pitch.

Instead, the players most central to that reset are still operating in knockout football.

Caicedo’s Ecuador role is the cleanest example. Read Chelsea has already assessed how his captaincy display against Germany strengthened his leadership case, but the next layer is more complicated.

Every additional knockout tie gives him more tournament rhythm, more authority and more fatigue.

Argentina’s route against Cape Verde keeps him on a glamorous stage at exactly the moment Chelsea need to settle his role, mood and tactical responsibilities under Alonso.

If Madrid-related noise continues around him, the club cannot afford a sluggish July handover.

Reece James started England’s first two matches before a hamstring issue ruled him out of the Panama game, according to the Guardian.

England still topped the group and moved into a last-32 tie with DR Congo, but James’ situation is exactly the kind of detail Chelsea’s medical team will monitor closely.

Chelsea have already had to plan around a large World Cup group.

The broader issue was clear in Read Chelsea’s earlier pre-season workload piece, but the knockout stage sharpens it because the returns will now be staggered.

Enzo brings a maximum group-stage load. Caicedo brings captaincy responsibility and heavy Ecuador minutes.

James brings knockout qualification mixed with another hamstring-management question.

Gusto and Hato remain tied to France and the Netherlands, while Penders and Paez are still absorbing tournament environments before club reintegration.

That is a spine issue, not a fringe issue.

Alonso needs automatisms in possession, spacing around the double pivot, clearer full-back behaviour and pressing triggers from midfield.

Those details do not bed in properly when key players arrive in drips after a major summer tournament.

Players returning from knockout football can bring competitive sharpness that closed-door friendlies cannot replicate.

Caicedo captaining Ecuador through pressure games matters. Enzo playing high-leverage minutes for Argentina matters.

Gusto and Hato absorbing tournament detail also helps Chelsea’s defensive reset.

But Chelsea cannot treat every tournament minute as clean preparation.

Alonso must decide who returns straight into tactical work, who needs a genuine pause and who can handle August without creating an avoidable injury bill by September.

That is where the James situation feels central.

If Chelsea’s captain carries a World Cup hamstring warning, the club’s right-sided structure becomes more than a selection debate.

It becomes an availability question that touches Gusto, the wider defensive rebuild and the need for control from midfield.

Read Chelsea has already looked at James’ captaincy test under Alonso, and the injury layer now makes that test sharper.

This is the hidden cost of a strong international footprint.

Chelsea want players good enough to survive deep into tournaments.

Alonso now has to make sure that status does not leave his first league weeks short of the very control those players are meant to provide.
